topicName: The Internet and the World Wide Web
description: An introduction to the Internet and the World Wide Web, covering connection requirements, web browsers, search engines, URLs, web pages, hyperlinks, and the uses, advantages and disadvantages of the internet.

options.text: A single computer that stores all the world's information
A global network that connects millions of computers together
A program used only for sending email
A device used to print web pages

mcq.explanation: The Internet is a worldwide network of interconnected computers and networks that share information and resources.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following best describes the World Wide Web (WWW)?

options.text: The physical cables that link computers
A collection of websites and web pages accessed through the Internet

mcq.explanation: The World Wide Web is a service on the Internet made up of linked web pages and websites that users can view using a browser.

mcq.questionText: Which program is used to access and display web pages on the Internet?
mcq.explanation: A web browser, such as Google Chrome or Mozilla Firefox, is software used to find, view and navigate web pages.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is an example of a search engine?
mcq.explanation: Google is a search engine that helps users find information on the web by typing in keywords.

mcq.questionText: What does the abbreviation URL stand for?
mcq.explanation: URL stands for Uniform Resource Locator, which is the unique address of a web page or resource on the Internet.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is needed to connect a computer to the Internet?
mcq.explanation: A modem is a device that connects a computer to the Internet by converting signals between the computer and the network line.

mcq.questionText: A company that provides Internet access to users is called a/an:
mcq.explanation: An Internet Service Provider (ISP) is a company that supplies Internet connection services to homes, schools and businesses.

mcq.questionText: A clickable word or image that takes you to another web page is called a:
mcq.explanation: A hyperlink is text or an image that, when clicked, links the user to another web page or website.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a use of the Internet for e-services?
mcq.explanation: Online banking is an e-service that lets users carry out transactions such as paying bills over the Internet.

mcq.questionText: The first page that appears when you open a website is known as the:
mcq.explanation: The home page is the main or opening page of a website that usually links to the other pages of the site.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a disadvantage of using the Internet?
mcq.explanation: The Internet can spread viruses and malware, which is one of its disadvantages along with privacy risks and harmful content.

options.text: A collection of related web pages stored under one domain name
A printer connected to the Internet

mcq.explanation: A website is a group of related web pages that share a common domain name and are accessed over the Internet.

mcq.questionText: In the URL http://www.necta.go.tz, the part 'go.tz' shows that the site is:
mcq.explanation: The domain part 'go.tz' indicates a government organisation in Tanzania, where 'go' means government and 'tz' is the country code for Tanzania.

mcq.questionText: Which Internet service allows people to send and receive electronic messages?
mcq.explanation: Email (electronic mail) is an Internet service used to send and receive messages between users quickly.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Internet from the World Wide Web?

options.text: They are exactly the same thing
The Internet is the network of computers, while the Web is a service of linked pages that runs on it
The Web is the hardware, while the Internet is the software
The Internet only works without the Web

mcq.explanation: The Internet is the global network infrastructure, while the World Wide Web is one of the services that uses the Internet to share linked web pages.

fib.questionText: A global network that connects millions of computers worldwide is called the _____.
fib.explanation: The Internet is the worldwide system of interconnected computer networks.

fib.questionText: Software used to access and view web pages is called a web _____.
fib.explanation: A web browser such as Chrome or Firefox displays web pages for the user.

fib.questionText: A program that helps users find information on the web by typing keywords is called a search _____.
fib.explanation: A search engine like Google returns a list of web pages matching the keywords entered.

fib.questionText: The unique address of a web page on the Internet is called a _____.
fib.explanation: URL stands for Uniform Resource Locator, the address that identifies a web resource.

fib.questionText: A clickable text or image that links one web page to another is called a _____.
fib.explanation: Hyperlinks connect web pages, allowing users to move between them with a click.

fib.questionText: A company that provides users with access to the Internet is called an Internet Service _____.
fib.explanation: An Internet Service Provider (ISP) supplies Internet connections to customers.

fib.questionText: The device that converts computer signals so they can travel over a telephone or network line is called a _____.
fib.explanation: A modem modulates and demodulates signals to connect a computer to the Internet.

fib.questionText: The main or opening page of a website is known as the _____ page.
fib.explanation: The home page is usually the first page seen and links to the rest of the website.

fib.questionText: Electronic mail, which is used to send messages over the Internet, is commonly abbreviated as _____.
fib.explanation: Email is a fast way of sending and receiving messages electronically over the Internet.

fib.questionText: A collection of related web pages stored under one domain name is called a _____.
fib.explanation: A website groups related web pages together under a single domain.

tf.questionText: The Internet and the World Wide Web mean exactly the same thing.
tf.explanation: The Internet is the network of computers, while the Web is a service of linked pages that runs on the Internet.

tf.questionText: A web browser is used to view web pages.
tf.explanation: Web browsers such as Chrome and Firefox are designed to display web pages.

tf.questionText: Google is an example of a web browser.
tf.explanation: Google is mainly a search engine; Google Chrome is the web browser made by the same company.

tf.questionText: A URL is the unique address of a web page.
tf.explanation: A Uniform Resource Locator (URL) identifies the exact location of a resource on the web.

tf.questionText: A modem is one of the requirements needed to connect to the Internet.
tf.explanation: A modem helps connect a computer to the Internet through a network or telephone line.

tf.questionText: Hyperlinks can only be text and never images.
tf.explanation: Both text and images can act as hyperlinks that take the user to another page.

tf.questionText: Online learning is one of the educational uses of the Internet.
tf.explanation: The Internet supports e-learning, allowing students to study and access materials online.

tf.questionText: Spreading computer viruses is an advantage of using the Internet.
tf.explanation: The spread of viruses is a disadvantage of the Internet, not an advantage.

tf.questionText: An Internet Service Provider (ISP) supplies Internet access to users.
tf.explanation: ISPs are companies that provide Internet connection services to homes, schools and businesses.

tf.questionText: A website is made up of one or more related web pages.
tf.explanation: A website is a collection of related web pages stored under one domain name.

summary.correctAnswer: A global network connecting millions of computers worldwide.
summary.explanation: It links networks together so they can share information and resources.

summary.questionText: Definition of the World Wide Web
summary.correctAnswer: A service of linked web pages and websites accessed through the Internet.
summary.explanation: The Web runs on the Internet and is viewed using a browser.

summary.correctAnswer: Software used to find, view and navigate web pages.
summary.explanation: Examples include Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox and Microsoft Edge.

summary.correctAnswer: A tool that helps users find information on the web using keywords.
summary.explanation: Examples include Google, Bing and Yahoo.

summary.correctAnswer: Uniform Resource Locator, the unique address of a web page.
summary.explanation: It tells the browser exactly where to find a resource.

summary.questionText: Requirements to connect to the Internet
summary.correctAnswer: A computer, a modem, an ISP and a communication line or signal.
summary.explanation: These work together to give a device access to the Internet.

summary.correctAnswer: A clickable text or image that links to another web page.
summary.explanation: Hyperlinks allow easy navigation between pages and sites.
People use it to find information, study, send messages and access online services.

summary.correctAnswer: Fast access to information, easy communication and online services.
summary.explanation: It saves time and connects people across the world.

summary.correctAnswer: Spread of viruses, privacy risks, harmful content and online fraud.
summary.explanation: Users must take care to stay safe and protect their information online.

hoq.questionText: A student types a question into Google, gets a list of links, and clicks one to open a page about photosynthesis. Which sequence of tools and concepts did the student use, in the correct order?

options.text: Search engine to find results, then a hyperlink to open the web page in the browser
Web browser to find results, then a modem to open the page
URL to search keywords, then an ISP to display the page
Hyperlink to search, then a search engine to open the page

hoq.explanation: The search engine returns results for the keywords, and clicking a hyperlink in the browser opens the chosen web page.

hoq.questionText: A school in a rural area has computers but cannot access any websites. The computers, browsers and power are all working. Which missing requirement is the MOST likely cause?

options.text: There is no Internet connection from an ISP
The browsers are not search engines
The web pages have no hyperlinks

hoq.explanation: Without a connection supplied by an ISP (through a modem and a network signal), the computers cannot reach any website even if everything else works.

hoq.questionText: Two URLs are given: http://www.example.ac.tz and http://www.example.co.tz. What can you correctly conclude about the type of organisations they belong to?

options.text: Both belong to government offices in Tanzania
The first is an academic institution and the second is a commercial company, both in Tanzania
Both are personal blogs hosted outside Tanzania
The first is commercial and the second is academic

hoq.explanation: In these URLs 'ac' means academic and 'co' means commercial, while 'tz' is the country code showing both are based in Tanzania.
